about: The stage's story, as data (stage/stage.js reads it). One scene tells one story; each step adds one thing and is cumulative. From Dinis's arc to storytelling.1 (12 Nov 2026, 01:18 UTC): the five altitudes; the same privileges; policies; runs that cannot reach the asset; the mesh against one agent per asset; scale; cost. Numbers come from the run files; scenes on sim: graphs are labelled SIMULATED on screen. storytelling.1 and swarm.1.designer may edit this file: keys are documented in stage/README.md.

scenes.title: Mandate, reach, gap
scenes.say: Three words for the rest of the demo. Mandate: what a unit is asked to do. Reach: what its process can actually touch. The gap between them is where things go wrong.
scenes.cue: Reach is measured: swarm.1's own container, before any policy (harness E01, 01:37 UTC).

card.mandateLabel: Mandate: one prompt in, one answer out
reach: unshare, setpriv, strace, iptables, nft, useradd

steps.caption: A model call's mandate: one prompt in, one answer out. No tools.

steps.label: reach

card.mandateLabel: Mandate: one prompt in, one answer out
reach: unshare, setpriv, strace, iptables, nft, useradd

steps.caption: The process it ran in could reach all of this. Measured, not assumed.

steps.label: the gap

card.mandateLabel: Mandate: one prompt in, one answer out
reach: unshare, setpriv, strace, iptables, nft, useradd

steps.caption: Reach minus mandate: the gap. Every incident lives there.

card.title: Two ways to close it
lines: Shrink the reach: one policy per process (the harness).
Move the work where the reach never was: a GitHub Action, a model provider.

scenes.title: One agent, five altitudes
scenes.say: A real run from last night: one agent doing six of the storm site's scheduled jobs. Watch what one agent turns into.

steps.label: you and the agent
steps.caption: You ask one agent (A3) to do a job. It has memory, tools and its own wake.

steps.label: loops
steps.caption: It starts loops (A2): read, ask, check, retry. Six of them, one per job.

steps.label: model calls
steps.caption: Each loop calls a model (A1): one prompt in, one answer out. Eight calls, on OpenRouter.

steps.label: code
steps.caption: And code runs (A0): six code units read the public storm data. 30 units in all, from one request.

steps.label: by colour
steps.caption: Five altitudes, one colour each. The same job; very different powers needed at each level.

scenes.title: Everybody can reach everything
scenes.say: Today, everything an agent starts runs with the agent's privileges. Connect the agent to your systems and see who can reach them.

steps.label: the run
steps.caption: The same run: one agent, its loops, its calls, its code.

steps.label: connect the agent
steps.caption: The agent is connected: Gmail and Calendar (simulated assets; the findings are riskmandate.ai's).

steps.label: who can reach them?
steps.caption: Who can reach them? Every loop, every model call, every line of code. Everybody.

steps.label: send, not draft
steps.caption: And holding the credential means it can send, not just draft. A grant is user-shaped, never data-shaped (riskmandate.ai).

steps.label: one goes wrong
steps.caption: What could happen: one prompt injection in the data, and that code holds the agent's credential.

scenes.title: A send button is not a mandate
scenes.say: RiskMandate's published findings on Gmail and Calendar: the grants are user-shaped, so an agent that may draft may also send, and an agent that may edit your calendar can do damage nobody can undo.

card.title: A send button is not a mandate
lines: Mandate: read and draft, never send. Grant: includes send, behind a setting the account can flip.
“The narrowest permission that lets it read one message lets it read every message.”
Calendar keeps deleted events for 30 days, and documents no way to get back an edited one.
A line in the agent's instructions is “a rule in prose, enforced by nobody.”

scenes.say: RiskMandate puts a policy on each unit: what it may reach, at its altitude.

scenes.title: Run it where the assets are not
scenes.say: A real run from tonight. The agent only commits a signed request; a GitHub Action runs the loops; OpenRouter runs the calls. Neither is connected to your assets.

steps.label: a signed request
steps.caption: The agent commits a signed request. That is all it does.

steps.label: the push starts an Action
steps.caption: The push starts a GitHub Action: a different place, with no access to your systems.

steps.label: the work runs there
steps.caption: 36 model calls and 24 loops run there, and on OpenRouter.

steps.label: can they reach the assets?
steps.caption: Can any of them reach Gmail or Calendar? No: they run where those are not connected. Don't hope the agent behaves: make the dangerous thing unreachable.

scenes.title: Five agents, every one wired to everything
scenes.say: People struggle with five agents, ten agents. Why: it is a mesh. Every agent has every connector.

scenes.title: One process, one policy, six probes
scenes.say: SHarness puts one child process under one deny-all policy. Six probes: read allowed; writing, the network, memory and the rest refused. Measured in swarm.1's container at 01:37 UTC.

card.title: An agent's process, before any policy
lines: uid 0, every capability, no seccomp, no no_new_privs.
iptables, useradd and strace within reach.
The whole internet through the session proxy.

steps.label: six probes

card.title: After: one child process under policy “hello” (deny-all)

steps.caption: Six probes, six held. Not a promise: a measurement.

card.title: What this policy does not cover yet
lines: Unix-domain sockets by path (no Landlock rule exists); the environment variables the process inherits; UDP, unless the empty network namespace applied.

card.title: The check runs inside the agent

rows.who: the agent (tricked by a page it read)

steps.label: tricked

card.title: The check runs inside the agent

rows.who: the agent (tricked by a page it read)
rows.ask: forward the inbox to a stranger

scenes.title: A check outside the process
scenes.say: SHarness puts the check outside the process: the kernel refuses, whatever the process was told. Real probes, swarm.1's container, 01:37 UTC.

steps.label: six asks, one policy

card.title: The check runs outside: the kernel, under one policy

steps.caption: Each ask meets the policy outside the process. Read: allowed. Write, network, memory: refused. Six of six held.

scenes.title: Who controls what they can do?
scenes.say: Governance: the honest line is that most rules observe and three enforce. That was a choice.

card.title: Who controls what they can do?
lines: Deny by default: one written grant per role and agent (45 agents in abp/policies.json v0.4.1).

lines.text: 12 core rules · 3 enforced · the rest observed

lines: Enforced by a hook: push to dev only (R5), never print a key (R8), commit only under your own name (R9).
The rest observe and log, by Dinis's choice: we learn first, and the log shows what each rule would have blocked.
